patch.value: GH-1703: pm context spends a third of its default output on a fixed omission receipt whose restore hints are all --section <name>

GH-1703 (filed 2026-11-11). Every default pm context call ends with an omission_receipt listing the ten sections the default projection leaves out, one row each, and every restore hint is the plain --section name form. Measured on a fresh two-item tracker: default TOON 1,449 B with a 505 B receipt (35 percent), --json 2,733 B with 684 B. The receipt is identical on every default call, so it is a fixed cost at the start of every session and the largest block on small trackers. Proposal: when the omitted set is exactly the documented default, emit one compact line of omitted section names plus a single restore template; keep the per-row table only for rows whose restore command is not derivable from the name (a budget cut, a truncated list, a requested section that could not be served); apply the same rule to other omission receipts whose restore hints are derivable from the row name.

When the omitted set equals the documented default, the receipt is one compact line of names plus a single restore template; Rows whose restore command is not derivable from the name keep the per-row form; Other omission receipts with name-derivable hints follow the same rule, and the receipt contract stays parseable
The default context receipt costs about 150 B
The default receipt is 505 B, 35 percent of output on a small tracker
